requirement.statement: The Kon parser SHALL NOT crash when a `^` suffix-complement token appears in a trailing / end-of-stream position; it SHALL either parse the construct or emit a clear diagnostic, and SHALL NOT throw an internal "End of stream" / null-dereference error.

suite.name: Caret suffix at end of stream

case.given: Kon source ends with an atom immediately followed by `^`, e.g. `a^`, `(a^)`, or `a^b`
case.when: The parser enters the `^` suffix-complement branch
case.then: The parser SHALL NOT throw the internal "End of stream" error (observed at `KnConverter.Kon.Parser.Parse("a^")`) and SHALL produce a node or a clear diagnostic

requirement.statement: The Kon parser SHALL NOT silently truncate a hyphenated symbol or knot head. A `#`-symbol such as `#foo-bar` SHALL NOT collapse to a bare `#`, and a knot head such as `foo-bar` SHALL NOT silently drop the `-bar` remainder. The parser SHALL parse the full intended token, or reject it with a diagnostic — never discard part of it silently.

case.given: Kon source contains a `#`-symbol with a hyphen, e.g. `#foo-bar`
case.then: The parser SHALL NOT produce a bare `#` word that silently discards `foo-bar` (current observed behavior)

case.given: Kon source contains a knot head with a hyphen, e.g. `(foo-bar 1 2)`
case.when: The parser reads the knot core
case.then: The parser SHALL NOT silently reduce the core to `foo` and drop `-bar` without any diagnostic (current observed behavior)

requirement.statement: A double-quoted interpreted string SHALL allow a `\(...)` interpolation whose embedded expression itself contains a double-quoted string literal, or SHALL reject it with a clear diagnostic. The inner `"` SHALL NOT prematurely terminate the outer string and silently garble the parse.

case.given: A double-quoted string with an interpolation whose expression contains a double-quoted literal, e.g. an interpolation that calls a string function with `"a"` and `"b"` arguments
case.when: The parser reads the outer string
case.then: The inner double quotes SHALL NOT prematurely close the outer string and produce a garbled map-shaped result; the construct SHALL parse correctly or be clearly rejected

requirement.statement: Non-ASCII characters (e.g. CJK) SHALL be usable as identifiers / bare words, or SHALL be clearly documented as unsupported. The lexer SHALL NOT throw a bare "Invalid Token" for an otherwise well-formed non-ASCII word outside string literals.

case.given: A non-ASCII word such as a CJK identifier appears outside a string literal
case.then: The lexer SHALL produce an identifier token (or a clear, documented diagnostic), not the generic "Invalid Token" error it currently throws (the Identifier regex is ASCII-only; non-ASCII is only accepted inside string literals)
